description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's Malawi Country Programme works to strengthen the trade competitiveness and regional integration of one of Southern Africa's most trade-constrained landlocked economies, operating along the Nacala, Beira, and Dar es Salaam corridors since 2020. The Programme targets three interconnected priorities: reducing the time and cost of trade through corridor-based facilitation measures, digital trade solutions, including an electronic data exchange system linking the Malawi Revenue Authority with Tanzania's customs platform and the development of the Lilongwe Dry Port to improve inland logistics access; strengthening export competitiveness in high-potential value chains, particularly mango and macadamia, through support for internationally recognised testing and certification at the Malawi Bureau of Standards under SADCAS accreditation and the development of over 30 crop-specific export standards; and promoting inclusive trade by supporting small-scale cross-border traders and advancing digital tools such as the MCCCI Single Digital Portal, which allows traders to obtain Certificates of Origin and other trade documents online, reducing compliance costs and administrative burden
Lilongwe is the capital city of Malawi
Mchinji is a border town in Malawi
Songwe is a border town in Malawi

provider-org.narrative: UK - Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.

title.narrative: Time taken to test, inspect and issue certificate of conformity

comment.narrative: Based on a baseline study conducted at the time
15% Reduction in time (days and hours) to test, inspect &/or issue certificates of conformity for macadamia in Malawi

•Accredited laboratory tests expanded from 4 to over 180.•SPS laboratory testing turnaround time reduced from 90 days to 30 days.•Estimated SPS testing costs reduced by approximately 68%, improving affordability for exporters.

Average testing costs declined from approximately USD 311 to USD 100 per sample substantially reducing reliance on foreign laboratories while improving export compliance and market access for Malawian producers.

title.narrative: Efficient trade through innovative digital technologies
Time taken to review, issue and collect the certificate of origin

comment.narrative: 83% reduction in issuance of Certificates of Origin from a maximum of 72 hours in 2024 to a maximum of 12 hours in 2026 following digitising of the Certificate of Origin (CoO) system through MCCCI

title.narrative: Percentage increase in trade between Malawi and Tanzania through Electronic Data Exchange System.

comment.narrative: 35% increase in trade between Malawi and Tanzania to $580 million in five months after the Malawi Revenue Authority and Tanzania Revenue Authority adopted an Electronic Data Exchange System linking their customs systems TANCIS for TRA and ASYCUDA World for MRA, providing custom officers real time access to one another’s declarations and risk profiles.

title.narrative: Trade processes, procedures, systems and regimes improved
Average border crossing time for heavy cargo trucks: Mchinji

comment.narrative: 43% reduction in average heavy cargo truck border crossing time at the Mchinji border from 48 hours to 27 hours following operationalisation of the Mchinji OSBP, implementation of coordinated border management, and customs modernisation with the ASYCUDA system.

title.narrative: Time (days/hours) associated with customs processes, including export customs processing time in Mchinji

comment.narrative: Mchinji: Import customs processing time reduced by 45.5% (2.2 to 1.2 hours), while export customs processing time reduced by 91.6% (8.3 to 0.7 hours).
